stimulus:
Shards (unordered, unexplained):

- lacquer cracking into craquelure as the underlayer shrinks, so the failure pattern records the history of drying
- a ferry pilot reading standing waves off a river bar to infer a hidden sandbank
- sourdough starters that keep a community alive through periodic discarding
- the moiré that appears only when two regular grids are slightly misaligned
- bell founders tuning by shaving metal from the inside lip, not by adding any
- lichens: two kingdoms, one body, boundary negotiated daily
- a tide table kept by a village that has no moon calendar, only knots in rope
- the ear's cochlea performing a Fourier transform in a coiled, fluid-filled shell
- mycelial networks rerouting after a cut, with no central map
- negative space in a woodblock print doing half the carving work
- a locksmith who listens to what the lock refuses to do
- salt deliberately added to ice to make it colder, not warmer
- a pidgin becoming a creole when children inherit it
- kintsugi: the repair is the most valuable part
- an auction in which the losing bids are what carry the information
- fog nets harvesting water from air that never rains

Now, before answering the question below, pick three shards that seem least related to it. For each, extract the underlying mechanism in one sentence. Then use those mechanisms, not their imagery, to generate proposals that a standard literature review would not suggest. Reject your first three obvious ideas.

Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Selective subtraction test (inner-lip shaving)
ideas.description: Mechanism borrowed from bell tuning: the state is set by removing material, not adding it. Instead of overexpressing AP-1, use acute degron-mediated removal (dTAG/AID of FOS/JUN family members, or dominant-negative A-Fos) at defined times after a transient stimulus, and measure whether the primed transcriptional response and chromatin accessibility at AP-1 sites persist, decay, or collapse. This tests whether AP-1 is required to maintain the memory or only to establish it.

ideas.title: Memory read out from the 'failed' sites (losing-bid information)
ideas.description: Mechanism borrowed from auctions: the information is in the bids that lose. After a first stimulus, use ATAC/CUT&RUN for AP-1 and pioneer-factor co-binding to identify motifs that were occupied or opened but did NOT lead to transcription (poised or non-productive sites). Test whether these silent-but-marked sites predict the magnitude of a second-stimulus response better than the sites that were active, using held-out genes and a predictive model.

ideas.title: Misalignment interference test (moiré)
ideas.description: Mechanism borrowed from moiré: a pattern emerges only from slight offset between two regular structures, so it reveals offsets invisible in either alone. Present two stimuli with varied timing and dose offsets (e.g., pulsed ERK/JNK inputs with different periods) while live-imaging AP-1 reporters and FOS/JUN dynamics at single-cell level. Look for beat-like interference in the second response that depends on the offset, which would show history-dependent encoding in AP-1 dynamics rather than simple state.

ideas.title: Single-cell lineage-tracked memory persistence
ideas.description: Barcode or live-track cells through a stimulus, and let them divide without stimulus. Use sister-cell concordance of AP-1 target expression and accessibility, versus random pairs, over several divisions to quantify heritability and half-life. Pair with mitotic bookmarking assays (live imaging and CUT&RUN on mitotic chromosomes) to see whether AP-1 stays bound through mitosis.

ideas.title: Sufficiency by site-specific rewriting
ideas.description: Use CRISPR to mutate individual AP-1 motifs (or dCas9-based recruitment and displacement of AP-1) at a few endogenous enhancers whose primed state is known. Then test whether memory of the prior stimulus at that locus is lost while neighbouring loci keep it. Combine with an orthogonal epigenetic readout (H3K27ac, nucleosome remodeling by BAF) to determine whether AP-1 itself or downstream chromatin marks carry the memory.
